\chapter{Wind, Cloud, and Rain: No New Signs}
\label{ch:mw-weather-three}
\hlchaptermodality{16}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can recognise, say, read, and write wind, cloud, and rain using only signs already secured in earlier chapters.}

Three source-attested weather nouns begin by ear, reuse the established script inventory, and finish in four separately scored skills without claiming a weather conversation is complete.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[havā]{Hear \emph{havā} — wind}

\label{lesson:MW-C11-hear-hawa}



\begin{quote}
Recall the five-word travel payoff, say home, then write \textbf{\mw{नाम}}, \textbf{\mw{पत्नी}}, and \textbf{\mw{बाजार}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{havā} — \textbf{wind}
\end{quote}

Listen once, then say the two light beats. Keep the meaning in your ear; the spelling waits for the next lesson even though every sign is already familiar.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-7-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 7}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[havā]{\mw{हवा} — wind on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C11-hawa}



\begin{quote}
Say wind and money, write \textbf{\mw{घर}}, then form \textbf{\mw{ह}}, \textbf{\mw{व}}, and \textbf{\mw{ा}} once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{ह}} + \textbf{\mw{वा}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{हवा}} — \emph{havā} — wind
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{हवा}}. No new sign has been added.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-7-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 7}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bādal]{Hear \emph{bādal} — cloud}

\label{lesson:MW-C11-hear-baadal}



\begin{quote}
Say and write wind, then recall temple, hand, maternal grandmother, and the \textbf{\mw{ै}} mark in \textbf{\mw{है}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{bādal} — \textbf{cloud; clouds}
\end{quote}

Hear the long first vowel. Say the sky word once without looking at any script.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-7-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 7}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bādal]{\mw{बादल} — cloud on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C11-baadal}



\begin{quote}
Say cloud, wind, and market. Write \textbf{\mw{नाना}} and the known my-name line ending in \textbf{\mw{है}}, then recall \textbf{\mw{ब}}, \textbf{\mw{ा}}, \textbf{\mw{द}}, and \textbf{\mw{ल}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{बा}} + \textbf{\mw{दल}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{बादल}} — \emph{bādal} — cloud
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write the two chunks. Check that only the first syllable carries \textbf{\mw{ा}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-7-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 7}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[barsāt]{Hear \emph{barsāt} — rain}

\label{lesson:MW-C11-hear-barsaat}



\begin{quote}
Say and write cloud and wind, contrast \emph{thāro} with \emph{mhāro}, then recall husband and write money.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{barsāt} — \textbf{rain; rainfall}
\end{quote}

Listen for the long final vowel. Say the weather word once from a rain cue.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-7-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 7}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[barsāt]{\mw{बरसात} — rain on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C11-barsaat}



\begin{quote}
Say rain and wind, recall the travel payoff, write \textbf{\mw{थ}}, then form \textbf{\mw{ब}}, \textbf{\mw{र}}, \textbf{\mw{स}}, \textbf{\mw{ा}}, and \textbf{\mw{त}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{बर}} + \textbf{\mw{सात}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{बरसात}} — \emph{barsāt} — rain
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{बरसात}}. Check that \textbf{\mw{ा}} sits only in the final chunk.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-7-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 7}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Retrieve wind, cloud, and rain}

\label{lesson:MW-R11-weather-three}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\mw{घ}}, \textbf{\mw{ज}}, \textbf{\mw{बच्चा}}, and \textbf{\mw{थारो}}, then say wife.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear the three words in mixed order, say each from its meaning, match three printed cards, then write all three from sound.

\section[Practice]{Payoff — three weather words in four skills}

\label{lesson:MW-C11-weather-three}



\begin{quote}
Say and write market and home, recall the twelve-label family payoff, then give the meanings of \emph{kāĩ} and \emph{hai} from the known name exchange.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
1. Identify three heard words. 2. Produce three words from meaning cues. 3. Match three printed cards to meanings. 4. Write all three heard words without a model.

Pass each skill separately.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-7-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 7}.
\end{tcolorbox}
